name: Double Leg Takedown
keyCorrections: If you keep getting guillotined: your head is too low or centered — keep head outside
If you keep getting sprawled on: your level change is too shallow or your entry is telegraphed
If you keep landing in guard: drive your hips through before dropping your knee
description: The double leg takedown adapted for no-gi BJJ, with emphasis on head position, guillotine defense, and chaining to other takedowns. Unlike wrestling double legs which prioritize finishing at all costs, BJJ double legs must account for front headlock counters, guillotines, and the opponent pulling guard. The modern no-gi double leg uses a head-outside position to protect the neck, combined with a deep penetration step and run-the-pipe finish.
shortInstruction: Level change, penetrate with head outside, drive through the hips, run the pipe to finish, and immediately defend the guillotine by keeping your head high.
summary: The BJJ-adapted double leg differs from wrestling in several ways: head position is outside (not inside) to protect the neck from guillotines; the finish prioritizes landing chest-to-chest in side control; and the entry often comes from arm drags, collar ties, or foot sweeps rather than straight shots. The key mechanical sequence is: level change → penetration step (head outside) → hip drive → run the pipe → land in a dominant pin. Guillotine defense must be instinctive — posture up immediately and peel the hands.
whyItWorks: Head-outside position protects the neck from guillotines and front headlocks
The double leg is the highest-percentage takedown in no-gi when combined with setup threats
Landing chest-to-chest gives immediate positional advancement to side control
Can be chained from foot sweeps, arm drags, and body lock entries
commonMistakes: Shooting with your head down — exposes the guillotine immediately
Dropping to your knees instead of driving through — gives up the finish
Stopping halfway — a partial double leg is worse than no attempt
Not chaining — a stuffed double leg should transition into a single or body lock
Landing in guard instead of driving to side control
coachingCues: Head outside, always — protects the neck
Level change before you step — don't telegraph
Drive through them, don't drop to your knees
Run the pipe — bring the far leg across your body
Chains: double → single → body lock → back take
safetySummary: Always keep your head to the outside to avoid guillotines
If you feel a guillotine, posture up immediately — do not continue driving
Sprawl defense: when sprawled on, protect your neck and recover to turtle or guard

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Double leg has 3 entries: Collar Tie → Arm Drag → Foot Sweep

decisionTree.action: Circle out to single leg or body lock
Posture up, peel the hands, and pass to side

moneyDetails: The double leg is the highest-percentage takedown in ADCC and no-gi competition
Modern no-gi double legs prioritize head safety over finishing at all costs
Nicky Rod and Kade Ruotolo use the double leg as their primary takedown entry
fixItFast: If guillotined: posture up and hand fight before anything else
If sprawled: circle to single leg or back out to reset
If stuck in guard: you landed too early — drive through next time
